linkedin.title: Personalised news is currently broken because it prioritises speed over substance.
linkedin.body:
Most news feeds today are designed to keep you scrolling by serving up whatever is loudest or most controversial. That is not personalisation. That is just an algorithm chasing engagement at the expense of your time and your peace of mind.

At Headlinne, we are building something different. The next step for personalised news is not about serving you more content. It is about serving you the right content based on your actual interests and your need for clarity. We are moving toward a model where the AI acts as a sophisticated editor rather than a content aggregator.

This means building tools that respect your intelligence. We are focusing on systems that can filter out noise and summarise complex topics without stripping away the nuance. The goal is to give you a complete picture of the day in minutes, not hours.

Technology should help us understand the world better, not just consume more of it. We are committed to making sure that remains the core of our roadmap.

reels.title: Google will now allow users to remove visible watermark from its AI generations
reels.hook: How to remove Google's AI labels

beats.caption: How to remove Google's AI labels
beats.detail: Here is what happens when you turn off the watermark on generated images.
beats.narration: Here is exactly how Google is changing the way it labels AI images.

beats.caption: Google changes AI labels
beats.detail: Users can now remove the visible watermark from AI-generated files.
beats.narration: Google now lets you turn off the visible watermark on images its AI creates.

beats.caption: The watermark toggle
beats.detail: You can switch off the visible label in your account settings.
beats.narration: It’s a simple switch in your settings that hides the logo on the image

beats.caption: Two types of ID
beats.narration: But this doesn't wipe everything. The invisible, machine-readable data

data.left_text: The logo you see on the image

beats.caption: Why it matters
beats.detail: Tech platforms can still detect that an image is AI-made.
beats.narration: So while the image looks cleaner to human eyes, software can still spot it.

beats.caption: AI images remain traceable
beats.narration: Basically, the AI images are still traceable.

reels.caption:
